result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would make it so people could reliably and deeply understand one another’s experiences and perspectives — a dramatic, widespread increase in genuine empathy and perspective-taking.

Why: many problems — violence, discrimination, policy short-sightedness, environmental destruction, and social isolation — stem from inability or unwillingness to see the world through others’ eyes. If more people could truly grasp the harms and hopes others face, decisions at personal, political, and institutional levels would tend to be kinder, more just, and more cooperative. Small acts of empathy scale into better governance, fairer economies, and stronger social bonds.

How it would show up: education and media that teach perspective-taking, cultural norms that value listening over winning, and technologies or practices that let people safely share lived experience. The result would be fewer needless harms and more collective will to solve shared challenges — a world where people treat each other as neighbors rather than obstacles.
